Investigation of Roadside Fine Particulate Matter Concentration Surrounding Major Arterials in Five Southern Californian Cities
venue: Journal of the Air & Waste Management Association
abstract: The built environment surrounding arterials affects the dispersion of vehicular emissions in urban areas, modifying the potential risks to public health. In order to study the influence of urban morphometry on flow and dispersion of vehicular fine particulate matter emissions, in the summer of 2008 field measurements were performed in major arterials located in five Southern Californian cities with different building geometries. In each city, local mean wind, turbulence, virtual temperature, roadside DustTrak Fine Particles (DTFP) concentration, and traffic flow data were collected in 2-hr measurement periods during morning and evening rush hours and lighter midday traffic, over a period of 3 days. The calculated Monin-Obukhov length, L, suggests that near-neutral and slightly unstable conditions were present at both street and roof levels. The nondimensional forms of turbulent wind and temperature fluctuations show,that the data at street level within the urban canopy can be represented using the Monin-Obukhov similarity theory. Generalized additive models were applied to analyze the impact of meteorological and traffic-related variables on fine particle concentrations at street level Compared to other variables, urban-scale background concentrations were the most important variables in all five models. The results confirmed that turbulent mixing in urban areas dominated the variation of roadside particle concentrations regardless of urban geometry. The distance from the local sites to the nearby monitoring stations affected model performance when urban-scale concentrations were used to predict middle-scale concentrations by generalized additive models (GAMs). A radius ofinfluence for background concentrations was 6-10 km. There were also relationships between concentration and other variables affecting the local components of the concentrations, such as wind direction, sensible heat flux, and vertical wind fluctuation, although the influences were much weaker Implications: The built environment surrounding major arterials affects the dispersion of vehicular emissions in urban areas, modifying the potential risks to public health. Dispersion of pollutants within the urban canopy is governed by flow and turbulence characteristics caused by building morphometry. Current dispersion models used for regulatory purposes have difficulties simulating the flow and dispersion for complex building cases, especially when fine resolution is needed. Urban planning strategies, such as limitation of building height, pedestrian-friendly community design, or zoning of building structures, modify concentrations of vehicular emissions in built environments surrounding major arterials, which may modify health risks for adjacent communities.
abstract_zh: 干道周边的建成环境影响城市中机动车排放的扩散，从而改变公众健康面临的潜在风险。为研究城市形态测量特征对机动车细颗粒物排放的流动与扩散的影响，我们于2008年夏季在南加州五座城市的主要干道上开展了实地测量，这五座城市的建筑几何形态各不相同。在每座城市，我们在为期3天的时间内，于早晚高峰及白天车流较少时段，以2小时为一个测量周期，收集了当地平均风、湍流、虚温、路边DustTrak细颗粒物（DTFP）浓度以及交通流量数据。计算得到的莫宁-奥布霍夫长度L表明，在街道和屋顶高度上均存在近中性和轻微不稳定的条件。湍流风速和温度脉动的无量纲形式表明，城市冠层内街道层面的数据可以用莫宁-奥布霍夫相似性理论来表示。我们应用广义可加模型（GAM）分析了气象和交通相关变量对街道层面细颗粒物浓度的影响。与其他变量相比，城市尺度背景浓度在全部五个模型中都是最重要的变量。结果证实，无论城市几何形态如何，城市中的湍流混合都主导着路边颗粒物浓度的变化。当利用广义可加模型以城市尺度浓度预测中尺度浓度时，当地站点与附近监测站之间的距离会影响模型表现。背景浓度的影响半径为6至10公里。此外，浓度与影响局部成分的其他变量之间也存在关系，如风向、感热通量和垂直风脉动，尽管这些影响要弱得多。启示：干道周边的建成环境影响城市中机动车排放的扩散，从而改变公众健康面临的潜在风险。城市冠层内的污染物扩散受建筑形态所引起的流动和湍流特征支配。目前用于监管目的的扩散模型在模拟复杂建筑情形下的流动与扩散时存在困难，尤其是在需要精细分辨率的情况下。城市规划策略，如限制建筑高度、以行人为本的社区设计或建筑结构分区，会改变干道周边建成环境中机动车排放的浓度，这可能进而改变邻近社区的健康风险。

title: The Declining Role of the Automobile and the Re-emergence of Place in Urban Transportation: The Past Will be Prologue
Can Built and Social Environmental Factors Encourage Walking Among Individuals with Negative Walking Attitudes?
venue: Journal of Planning Education and Research
abstract: We investigate whether the design of the built environment encourages walking above and beyond individuals’ attitudes toward walking. With data from a regional travel survey, we use regression analyses to examine differences in neighborhood walking trips among residents with positive and negative attitudes toward walking. The results show that built and social environment factors have a differential impact on walking trips depending on a person’s walking attitudes. Therefore, strategies to promote positive walking attitudes should be pursued in tandem with land use policies to encourage neighborhood walking.
abstract_zh: 我们考察了建成环境的设计是否能够促进步行，且其作用超出了个人对步行的态度。利用一项区域出行调查的数据，我们通过回归分析考察了对步行持积极和消极态度的居民在社区步行出行方面的差异。结果表明，建成环境与社会环境因素对步行出行的影响，因个人的步行态度不同而存在差异。因此，在推行土地利用政策以鼓励社区步行的同时，也应制定策略，以促进积极的步行态度。
